# 1 Enoch Chapter 106 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Birth of Noah (Appendix)

---

**1** Some time later, my son Methuselah arranged a marriage for his son Lamech. His wife became pregnant and gave birth to a son.

**2** The child's body was white as snow and flushed red as a blooming rose. The hair on his head, his long locks — white as wool. His eyes were extraordinary.

**3** When he opened his eyes, the light that poured out of them lit up the entire house like sunlight. The whole room blazed with brilliance.

**4** While he was still being held in the midwife's hands, he sat up and opened his mouth — and spoke to the Lord of Righteousness.

**5** His father Lamech was terrified. He turned and ran to his own father, Methuselah.

**6** He said: "I have fathered a strange son — unlike anything human, more like the sons of the angels of heaven. His nature is completely different from ours. His eyes shoot out rays like the sun. His face is radiant.

**7** I'm beginning to think he didn't come from me at all. I think he came from the angels. And I'm afraid of what might happen in his days on the earth.

**8** Father, please — go to our ancestor Enoch. He lives with the angels. Ask him. He will tell you the truth."

**9** When Methuselah heard this from his son, he came to find me at the ends of the earth — he'd been told I was there. He called out, and I heard him, and I came. I said to him: "Here I am, my son. What brings you here?"

**10** He said: "I've come because something is weighing heavily on me. A troubling vision has driven me to you.

**11** My father — listen to me. Lamech's wife has given birth to a son like none that has ever been born. His nature is not human nature. His body — whiter than snow, redder than a blooming rose. His hair — whiter than white wool. His eyes like sunbeams. And when he opened his eyes, the whole house flooded with light.

**12** He sat up in the midwife's hands. He opened his mouth and blessed the Lord of heaven.

**13** Lamech is terrified. He ran to me. He cannot believe the child is really his — he thinks the boy looks like one of the angels of heaven. I've come to you, grandfather, to learn the truth."

**14** I, Enoch, answered him: "The Lord is about to do something new on the earth. I have already seen it in a vision. Let me tell you: in the days of my father Jared, some of the angels of heaven broke the command of the Lord.

**15** They are sinning still, transgressing the law — they have gone to women and slept with them, married some of them, fathered children with them.

**16** And on the earth there will be giants — born from flesh, not from spirit. A terrible punishment will fall on the earth, and the earth will be cleansed of all its impurity.

**17** Yes — a catastrophic destruction will sweep the whole earth. There will be a flood. A year of complete destruction.

**18** But this son who was just born to your family — he will survive. He will remain on the earth, and his three sons will be saved with him. When everyone else on earth dies, he will be kept safe.

**19** Now go. Tell your son Lamech: the child is truly his son — he need not fear. Name him Noah. Because Noah will be spared for you, and he and his sons will be rescued from the coming destruction — which will fall on the earth because of all the sin and all the unrighteousness that will reach its full measure in his days."

---

*PNEUMA notes: This is the most dramatic chapter in the Epistle's appendix — a birth story that reads like a folk tale crossed with apocalyptic prophecy. The infant Noah is luminous: his eyes light up the room, he immediately speaks to God, and his father runs away in terror. The double retelling (Lamech to Methuselah, Methuselah to Enoch) is a literary technique to build suspense. Enoch's calm, prophetic answer (vv. 14–19) places this extraordinary birth in the context of the Watcher sin and the coming Flood.*
